title: Types of conflict

match.reason: Neither bank point teaches the types of conflict (character against another person, nature, society or themselves); they cover how setting and events reveal character and how dialogue builds character, so no existing point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Types of conflict
card: Conflict is a struggle between a character and something that stands in their way. It gives a story its tension and keeps readers wanting to know what happens.
a struggle against another person, such as two rivals who both want the same prize.
a struggle against the natural world, such as a hiker caught in a blizzard.
Character vs society and character vs self

Against society is a struggle with the rules or attitudes of a group, such as a girl who challenges a town's ban on her sport. Against self is a struggle inside the character's own mind, such as a boy torn between telling the truth and protecting a friend.
draft.remember: Ask who or what the character is struggling against: another person, nature, society or themselves.

a.q: Priya spends the whole story fighting her own fear of speaking in public before a big speech. What type of conflict is this?
a.why: The struggle is inside Priya's own mind, so it is a conflict against self. It is not against another person, because nobody else is standing in her way.
a.clue: Where is the struggle happening: outside Priya or inside her?

b.q: In a short story, Tomas lives in a village where everyone must follow an old rule that bans anyone from leaving. He secretly plans to leave and is hunted by the villagers' leader. Which conflict is the main struggle against the rule?
b.why: The ban is a rule held by the whole village, so Tomas is struggling against society. The leader hunting him is a person, but the struggle with the rule comes from the group's expectations, not one person's dislike of him.
b.clue: Think about who made and enforces the rule that blocks Tomas.
